description: Amplifies or attenuates the spectrum by scaling every channel amplitude by gain, leaving frequencies untouched (content-verified: median amp ratio exactly 2.0 at gain 2 and 0.5 at gain 0.5 against the input's channel amps; gain 1.0 is a byte-identical passthrough). Static duration (2.0230 s from a 2.023 s analysis, 1.5209 from 1.5209), deterministic (runs 1.3 s apart byte-identical). Operates on PVOC analysis files (.ana).
musical_use: The level trim of the spectral domain - SoundThread frames it as the frequency-domain twin of its Gain node, and its main job is exactly that: pull a hot spectral chain down (gain < 1) so the eventual pvoc synth doesn't clip, or push a quiet intermediate up before a level-sensitive stage (focus, trace, suppress-style ops whose thresholds see channel amplitude). With a breakpoint file it becomes a spectral fade/envelope drawn directly on the analysis data - fade a sound in or out without touching the time domain, or duck the middle of a chain for a swell. gain 0 legally renders spectral silence (useful as the floor of a breakpoint fade).

gain.description: Amplitude multiplier applied to every analysis channel: < 1 attenuates, > 1 amplifies, 1.0 is a verified byte-identical no-op, 0 is legal (spectral silence). CDP-enforced 0 to 10000 ('-1' refused verbatim: 'Parameter[1] Value (-1.000000) out of range (0.000000 to 10000.000000)'; 10000 accepted) - SoundThread's 0.001-2 slider is an advisory subset. May vary over time via a breakpoint file (verified: a 0.1-to-4 ramp differs from both scalar-endpoint renders).

examples.description: Pull a hot spectral chain down before resynthesis (SoundThread default 0.8).
examples.expected_use: Same sound, 20% lower channel amplitudes - headroom for pvoc synth.

examples.description: Spectral fade-out drawn on the analysis data.
examples.expected_use: The sound fades to spectral silence across its duration without a time-domain envelope stage.

known_issues: gain 0 is accepted (renders all-zero channel amps) - deliberate silence, not an error; anything negative is refused.

Scaling is exact and frequency-transparent (amp ratio 2.0/0.5 verified channel-wise; gain 1.0 byte-identical) - there is no hidden normalisation or limiter, so large gains can push channel amps far above 1.0 and clip only at resynthesis.
